title: Workhuman vs BI Worldwide: [current_year] Comparison Guide
teaser: BI Worldwide vs. Workhuman: Compare features, pricing, integrations, global reach, and impact on employee engagement to choose the right platform.
bodyText: Employee recognition has become a necessity across different business structures, from healthcare to sales. As workloads increase and technology becomes more embedded in workflows, recognition plays a crucial role in supporting collaboration, alignment, and goal-setting — especially when taking on new challenges.  Workhuman and BI Worldwide stand out as intuitive employee recognition platforms with customizable pricing structures, but they're built for rather different workflows. Workhuman acts as a strategic recognition program with measurable impact and deeper insight, while BI Worldwide distinguishes itself by focusing on economic insights and sales incentives.  If you're comparing BI Worldwide and Workhuman to find a better fit for your business structure, this guide will help you make an informed decision. It will outline the key features and differences of both platforms, so you can choose with confidence.  Workhuman vs. BI Worldwide Platform Overview Workhuman at a Glance  BI Worldwide at a Glance  Positioned as a solution both for employee recognition and sales incentives, making it  a popular solution for motivating sales teams   Founded in 1950  and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, with over 40 sales offices and locations worldwide  Emphasizes measurable business outcomes, linking recognition directly to increased sales and other financial goals  Leverages  behavioral economics (BE),  which integrates psychological research with economic principles to prioritize sales and revenue alongside engagement and performance  The  BIW Gamification Platform  and other personalized systems structure recognition and rewards using points, leaderboards, and other game mechanics, leveraging behavioral, financial, and other data-driven insights  Enables  peer-to-peer (P2P) recognition  with immediate social feedback and with points-based reward and recognition programs  AI-powered systems, such as  Enhance  and  GoalQuest AI,  support key recognition processes, including drafting messages, identifying rewards, and setting personalized sales goals  Limited ability to surface meaningful, enterprise-grade insight about:  Feedback loops  Data fragmentation  Context-independent recognition  Comprehensive behavior  The  Rewards Marketplace  lets users choose from over one million rewards, including merchandise, experiences, and career development options  Integrations with common workplace tools, including Outlook, Teams, Slack, and IBM, support recognition insights  Limited customer or client reviews online reflect uncertainty about the platform's reliability  Feature Comparison: Workhuman vs. BI Worldwide   Recognition & Culture Building Workhuman   BI Worldwide  BIW Gamification Platform:  Personalized gamification drives engagement and motivation using familiar game mechanics. This strategic approach aims to encourage high-value actions and meaningful collaboration in a fun, engaging environment, whether you're tracking sales or onboarding. Game mechanics and strategies include:  Point and score systems  Leaderboards  Real-time dashboards  Progress bars  Badges and levels  Missions and tailored tasks  Built on behavioral economics:  BI Worldwide's recognition platform combines psychological and economic research to design programs that drive engagement, sales, and performance. This shifts programs beyond traditional incentives by treating motivation as a science and allowing leaders to consider both behavioral and financial insights when making decisions.  Actionable insights:  BE-backed research helps leaders craft recognition programs and messages that motivate direct action, such as by rewarding specific positive behaviors.  Context-independent recognition:  Recognition systems may not account for key variables that affect employees' performance and engagement, such as their location, team structure, or unique role requirements. This can limit the relevance and integrity of insights, potentially causing leaders to overlook key contributors.  Measurable business outcomes:  The program directly links recognition to financial goals and outcomes, such as increased sales and employee retention.  Peer-to-peer recognition:  BI Worldwide supports immediate peer recognition within its digital platform, encouraging social support and emotional connections. The platform also offers points-based P2P rewards programs that motivate employees to "shout out" to each other and work harder to receive positive recognition themselves.  Career development:  Mastery reward options enable employees to develop their own skills and strengths, such as through online courses, to support continuous career growth.  Limited focus on comprehensive behavior:  Many of BI Worldwide's employee recognition systems predominantly focus on averages among teams rather than offering a comprehensive understanding of how employees' needs differ.    Integrations & Tech Ecosystem Fit Workhuman  BI Worldwide Broad partnerships and integrations:  Partnerships with IBM, Ability Map, ProHabits, Quantum Workplace, and Workday allow BI Worldwide to function within businesses' existing systems.  Work tool integrations:  The platform also integrates with Slack, Microsoft Workplace, Outlook, Google Workspace, Chrome, Teams, Yammer, and other popular work tools. However, some of these integrations require you to use additional apps and tools, such as RecognitionNow DM.  Data fragmentation:  BI Worldwide's level of integration hinges on how synchronized your current systems already are. Fragmented data across different teams and locations can make reporting inconsistent and challenging, limiting the accuracy and integrity of insights.  Integrations across industries:  BI Worldwide is optimized to assist teams and integrate with tools across various industries such as agriculture, manufacturing, and retail.  Disconnect between surveys and results:  The program has gaps between the processes for administering employee surveys and sharing the results. This lack of integration makes it challenging for leaders to respond to survey results in an actionable way, especially within enterprise-level organizations.   Pricing & Cost-Effectiveness Workhuman  BI Worldwide  Custom pricing model designed for sales:  BI Worldwide uses a points-based pricing model customized around your business's unique goals and budget. Costs are flexible and specific to your program's design, but they steadily increase as your business scales.  Limited global price fluctuations:  Partnerships with global supplier networks help users avoid third-party markups and other price fluctuations, keeping program and reward costs generally consistent across international businesses and teams.  Pay-for-performance structures:  Certain reward systems, such as GoalQuest AI, leverage pay-for-performance rules that incentivize each employee's unique achievements. This means your program will likely cost more based on its success.  Disappointment with pricing options:  Online reviews indicate dissatisfaction with BI Worldwide's pricing models, with some segments or programs considered overpriced.  Impact on Engagement, Retention, and Morale Workhuman     BI Worldwide Tailored recognition insights:  Expert insights help leaders tailor recognition to each workforce's specific, complex needs. Specific, actionable recognition helps leaders reinforce desired behaviors and prompt change.  P2P rewards and points programs:  BI Worldwide offers points-based rewards programs for peer-to-peer recognition, encouraging stronger performances and higher engagement with the rewards program.  Personalized reward options:  A diverse marketplace of merchandise, experiences, and mastery rewards lets leaders and employees choose incentives tailored to each individual's unique interests. This can drive greater motivation and engagement, whether employees want to learn a new skill or book great seats at a concert.  Potential to overlook key contributors:  Context-independent recognition may overlook factors affecting employees' performance, leading to some employees being highlighted more than others within the recognition system.   AI and Product Innovation Workhuman   BI Worldwide Elevate Intelligence:  An AI-powered advanced behavior-change ecosystem combines incentives, recognition, and crucial data to help businesses celebrate achievements and strengthen desired behaviors. AI integrations simplify user experiences and allow leaders to personalize their programs around employees' unique needs and gaps.  Recognition Assistant:  A built-in AI assistant for Elevate Intelligence helps users write authentic recognition messages that reference specific achievements and suggest behaviors to expand upon. The assistant focuses on a few core areas of every message:  Biased language  Spelling and grammar  Clarity and specificity  Translations  GoalQuest AI:  A pay-for-performance rules structure that tracks each employee's unique sales data and grants rewards based on personalized goals. This AI system aims to give participants greater feelings of ownership over their workflows, usually at a greater program cost.   Global Reach and Capabilities Workhuman  BI Worldwide  Diverse reward selection:  BI Worldwide's Rewards Marketplace includes 800,000 merchandise options from Apple, Yeti, Bose, Ring, Xbox, and many more recognizable brands — as well as 350,000 experience rewards, such as hard-to-get game tickets, concert tickets, local tours, and sightseeing opportunities.  Global experiences and rewards:  The diverse marketplace selection ensures employees have options worldwide. This allows businesses to maintain equity across teams while keeping all employees engaged, regardless of where they live.  Minimal price markups:  Global supplier partnerships limit price fluctuations across regions, keeping program and reward costs equitable worldwide.  Worldwide mastery rewards:  In lieu of merchandise or experiences, the Mastery Marketplace offers over 17,000 worldwide reward options to help employees expand their skills and grow their careers. Employees can earn expenses-paid admission to skills training, language programs, wellness sessions, music lessons, cooking classes, and more, including virtual and remote options for global accessibility.   Customer Support Workhuman  BI Worldwide  Strategic partnership:  BI Worldwide aims to operate as more than a vendor for businesses, acting as a strategic partner in each business's success. BIW teams work closely with brands to understand their unique strengths and needs. From here, they implement customized solutions to drive impact and outcomes.  Phone number for immediate assistance:  Beyond text fields and standard communication methods, BI Worldwide offers a 1-800 number for immediate assistance with programs, orders, and rewards. title: The Service Award That Said Almost Nothing
teaser: A generic milestone gift. A gift card. And one anniversary that misses the mark. In this thoughtful piece, Cam explores why service awards so often let people down — and what employees actually remember years later.
bodyText: A few years ago, I was meeting a good friend for dinner after work. Let’s call her Jane. (Names and identifying details have been changed for privacy.) She was coming from picking up her mail, and when she sat down, she dropped a small cardboard package onto the table between us and laughed. “I think this is my ten-year service award.” I remember getting genuinely excited for her. Ten years at one company is a big deal, especially now. Ten years means you’ve made it through reorganizations, difficult managers, great teammates, stressful launches, unexpected opportunities, and all the tiny moments that slowly add up to a career. It means you stayed long enough to build history somewhere. I told her to open it. She peeled back the tape, pulled out the packing paper, and opened a branded box with her company logo across the top. For a second, there was a little anticipation around the whole thing. You could tell she was being casual but wanted it to feel meaningful. Inside was a plastic frame with her company’s logo and a neatly etched “10 Years.” Alongside it: a $100 Visa gift card and a brochure with a list of places where it could be used. She looked down at everything for a second, then flipped the brochure over like maybe she’d missed something.  I asked if there was a note. (There wasn’t.) Had her team reached out about the milestone? “No,” she said with a small laugh. “I guess even I kind of forgot about it.” So, I asked the obvious question: How did it feel? Her answer: “No one cares about stuff like that. The whole thing is lame.” But I don’t think she believed that. Because Jane had given a lot to that company over those ten years. She relocated for the role, took on entirely new responsibilities, worked across departments, mentored people, survived multiple reorganizations, and built relationships that shaped her career and probably a lot of other people’s careers, too. Jane certainly didn’t expect balloons to fall from the ceiling or some elaborate celebration. But ten years of your life feels like it should be acknowledged with a little more humanity than a plastic frame and an automated workflow. And I think a lot of people have had some version of that experience. When Recognition Misses the Moment What ultimately stayed with me about Jane’s award wasn’t the gift itself. It was the total absence of reflection. Here was a company investing real time and money into a program designed to celebrate loyalty, and it  landed somewhere between indifference and disappointment.  At first glance, it’s easy to assume no one cares. But that’s not true. Jane cares deeply about her company. About her team. About the years she’s invested. And her company clearly values her. They’ve supported her growth, recognized her achievements, and invested in her career. So, what broke? I’d say the moment did. No one paused to reflect on what those ten years had meant to Jane or her company. No stories from teammates. No reminder of the challenges she had overcome or the impact she had made. The experience came and went in less than five minutes, which felt strange considering it represented an entire decade of someone’s working life. Which is unfortunate, because anniversaries and milestones matter deeply to people. We instinctively celebrate time everywhere else in life. Birthdays, weddings, graduations, retirements, anniversaries, reunions — these moments give us an opportunity to stop, reflect, and reconnect with the people around us. They help us mark growth and shared experience. Service anniversaries should be some of the most meaningful moments in an employee’s journey.  Especially now, when so many employees are searching for connection and meaning at work, these moments carry more emotional weight than organizations sometimes realize. A service anniversary isn’t really about tenure alone. It’s about contribution, growth, relationships, resilience, and shared history. But in many organizations, Years of Service programs have been reduced to a date and a transaction. The Difference Between a Reward and a Memory I’ve experienced the opposite side of this myself. I’ve now been at Workhuman for nearly ten years, and my experience couldn’t be more different than my friend’s. At my 1-year, 3-year, 5-year, and 7-year milestones, I’ve found myself staying up past midnight, waiting for the moment my anniversary award would be posted. Not for the reward. For the  messages.  We use our own  Service Awards solution , and that means when the award arrives it’s full of messages. From my leaders. From my managers. And from my peers. Videos. Silly gifs. Pics I forgot someone ever took.  Each time I’ve hit a milestone, I’ve read through notes from teammates, reliving old projects, challenges, and moments I had long forgotten — projects we somehow survived together, difficult launches, funny mistakes, late nights, moments that shaped our careers in ways we didn’t recognize at the time. And each time, I’ve been reminded of the people behind the work. I can tell you, what stayed with me wasn’t the reward attached to the milestone. It was the feeling I had of belonging, and  mattering , to a whole lot of people in my life. That’s the difference.  The best milestone experiences create reflection and connection. They help employees see the impact they’ve had, not through a corporate message, but through the voices of the people they worked beside every day. Done well, those moments reinforce culture in a way that policies and presentations never really can. And that emotional layer matters a lot more than many organizations realize.   Milestones Matter More Than Companies Think  Service anniversaries  are one of the few moments every organization already has built into the employee experience. Nearly every large company has some version of a Years of Service program because tenure matters everywhere. Yet despite how universal these programs are, many still feel oddly disconnected from the humans they’re designed to celebrate. That creates a huge opportunity for HR leaders. Not necessarily to spend more money or create bigger rewards, but to rethink the experience itself. The organizations getting this right are designing moments that feel participatory, social, reflective, and deeply human. They’re creating opportunities for peers and managers to contribute stories, appreciation, and shared memories instead of simply triggering a transaction tied to a date in the HRIS. And the impact extends beyond the moment itself. When employees feel genuinely seen and valued, those experiences strengthen culture, deepen belonging, and reinforce connection to the organization. Small improvements in how recognition is delivered can completely change how employees experience the milestone. That’s something more organizations are starting to realize. Recognition isn’t really about the object. It’s about the emotional resonance surrounding the moment. At Workhuman, we believe milestone moments deserve more. Our Service Milestones experience (which is now available stand-alone to customers who don’t use Recognition) isn’t just about marking time. It’s about honoring the past, celebrating the present, and reinforcing connection for the future. When done right, these moments strengthen culture, deepen engagement, and turn tenure into something truly meaningful. At their best, these moments tell employees something simple but powerful: You mattered here.   Learn more about Workhuman’s  Service Milestones  solution here.
